name: RepairStep Open Box
author: repairstep

sections.description:
Returned, opened or demo units are money sitting on a shelf. RepairStep grades them (A – Like New to D – Fair), lists them back on your WooCommerce store at a discount, and records the sale when they sell. This companion plugin is the storefront half: it makes those listings look deliberate on your site.

What the plugin does

  • The offers box – a live “Open box available” box on the original product’s page whenever graded units are for sale, with current prices, strikethrough savings and availability. Sold out means it quietly disappears. Automatic placement next to Add to Cart on standard themes; page-builder sites (Divi, Elementor, …) place it exactly where they want it with the [repairstep_open_box] shortcode.
  • A purpose-built open box product page – your theme’s header, footer and fonts stay; the body becomes a deal-shaped layout: fixed gallery with tap-to-enlarge, a title banner in your accent colour, grade ladder, strikethrough pricing, the unit’s honest condition description and photos, and links to the other grades of the same product.
  • Three page designs to choose from – RepairStep’s purpose-built design, your theme’s own product template, or a hybrid where your theme renders the page and you place the deal pieces yourself with shortcodes ([repairstep_condition], [repairstep_other_grades], [repairstep_trust_note]).
  • One page per grade – every grade is its own product page with the grade in the title; identical units stack as quantity. Flawed grades always carry photos of the actual unit.
  • A free outlet page – every open box product joins the Open Box category automatically, giving you a ready-made outlet at /product-category/open-box/.
  • A settings page that answers questions – live status of your listings, a live preview of the offers box as you type, placement help that recognises your page builder, a built-in “How Open Box works” guide and troubleshooting.

Private by design

The plugin makes no external requests – no tracking, no phoning home, nothing loaded from other servers. It only reads product data that RepairStep writes to your store through the WooCommerce REST API keys you create. Prices and stock in the offers box are read live from WooCommerce on every page view.

Requires a RepairStep account

Listings themselves – grading, photos, pricing, which store a unit goes to, and the automatic close-out when a unit sells – are created and managed in RepairStep, a paid service for distributors and retailers who handle repairs, returns and open box stock. Without a RepairStep account the plugin simply renders nothing. Terms – Privacy policy.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin zip via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, and activate it.
  2. Connect your store in RepairStep (Settings → Integrations → WooCommerce) with WooCommerce REST API keys.
  3. That is all – offers appear wherever RepairStep lists units. Settings live under WooCommerce → RepairStep Open Box.
sections.faq:
Do I need a RepairStep account?

Yes. The plugin displays open box listings that RepairStep creates and manages on your store – grading, pricing, stock and the sale close-out all happen there. Without an account the plugin renders nothing.

Does the plugin send my data anywhere?

No. It makes no external requests at all. RepairStep connects to your store the other way around, through WooCommerce REST API keys you create and can revoke at any time.

The offers box is not showing – why?

The most common reasons, in order: no open box unit is live and in stock for that product (by design); Placement is set to manual with no shortcode placed; your page cache is showing an old copy – refresh it; or the unit was listed to a different store. The settings page’s Status panel and Troubleshooting section walk you through all of these.

The box shows at the top of the page instead of by Add to Cart

Your product pages are built with a page builder, so the standard WooCommerce position is not where it looks. Add the [repairstep_open_box] shortcode where you want the box – in a page or once in your builder’s product template – and set Placement to manual.

Can I change how the open box product page looks?

Yes – three ways, under WooCommerce → RepairStep Open Box: RepairStep’s purpose-built design (with your accent colour), your theme’s normal product template, or the hybrid mode where you place the condition block, other-grades list and trust note yourself with shortcodes.

Where do I change an open box price?

In WooCommerce, on the open box product itself – the sale price is the offer price, the regular price is the crossed-out “was” price. RepairStep picks the change up automatically.

What happens when a unit sells?

RepairStep records the sale automatically, including the sold price. When the last unit of a listing is gone, the open box product returns to draft and the offer disappears from the product page on its own.
sections.changelog:
1.5.6

  • Every shortcode and every box now escapes its HTML at the point of
    output, instead of relying on the pieces having been escaped where they
    were built. Covers [repairstep_open_box], [repairstep_other_grades] and
    the offers box rendered by the automatic placement.
  • The purpose-built deal page escapes the condition block through the same
    helper as the shortcode, which also restores the condition photo row’s
    layout – the generic filter had been stripping its CSS.

1.5.5

  • All styles and scripts are now loaded with the WordPress enqueue
    functions instead of inline tags, so they are cacheable and a theme or
    optimisation plugin can manage them. The only inline block left is the
    JSON-LD product data, which cannot be enqueued.
  • The merchant’s accent colour reaches the deal page as CSS custom
    properties, keeping the stylesheet itself static.
  • Hardening: the [repairstep_condition] shortcode now escapes the
    condition block before returning it, so markup in a product description
    cannot inject script into the page.

1.5.4

  • Deal-page template variables now carry the rsob_ prefix, so they can
    never collide with a theme’s or another plugin’s globals.

1.5.3

  • Text domain is now “repairstep”, matching the plugin’s directory slug.

1.5.2

  • Tested against WordPress 7.1.

1.5.1

  • Directory-listing preparation: full readme (description, FAQ,
    screenshots), and strict sanitisers on every saved setting.

1.5.0

  • Hybrid design mode: your theme renders the open box page and you place
    the deal pieces yourself with shortcodes – [repairstep_condition] (the
    condition block leaves the description and renders only where you put
    it), [repairstep_other_grades] and [repairstep_trust_note]. All three
    render nothing on normal products, so they can live in a shared
    page-builder product template.

1.4.0

  • The open box page design grows up: a title banner in your accent colour
    (new setting, with automatic light/dark text), a breadcrumb to the Open
    Box page, a proper gallery – fixed square window, thumbnails that swap
    the image in place, tap to enlarge – the trust note under the buy
    button, and Product structured data so search engines see price and
    availability.

1.3.0

  • One page per grade: newly listed grades each get their own open box
    product page, and each page shows an “Other grades available” strip
    linking to its siblings. Existing multi-grade listings keep working
    (including the grade cards) until they sell through.

1.2.0

  • Grade cards: when a deal has two or more grades in stock, the deal page
    shows one card per grade – its wording, price, availability and its own
    Add to basket – instead of a dropdown. Grades compare side by side.
  • Cart notices (“Added to basket”) now show on the deal page.

1.1.1

  • The settings page gains a “How Open Box works” guide: grading, listing
    (draft then publish), how units pool by grade, where prices are changed,
    what happens on sale or withdrawal, the outlet page, and the three rules
    that keep everything working.

1.1.0

  • The offers box shows at most four offers, cheapest first – when there are
    more, a final line links to the Open Box category page. The box no longer
    grows with inventory on products with many flawed-grade units.
  • Clearer settings copy throughout: placement is a two-option choice
    (Automatic / Manual) with descriptions that explain only the chosen mode,
    the deal page section speaks of the open box product page, and the
    troubleshooting answers are written in plain words.

1.0.9

  • The settings page grows up: a status panel (live deals, covered product
    pages, sold/withdrawn, newest listing, view-on-site links), a live preview
    of the offers box that follows your heading, note and layout as you type,
    placement help that recognises your page builder with a copy button for
    the shortcode, clearer deal-page copy, and a troubleshooting section.
  • “Settings” link on the Plugins list row.

1.0.8

  • New setting: automatic placement of the offers box can be switched off,
    for sites that place the shortcode themselves – for example once in a
    page-builder product template that covers every product.

1.0.7

  • The shortcode no longer renders while WooCommerce builds its schema.org
    data from the product description – that invisible render was consuming
    the once-per-page slot on products without a short description, leaving
    a builder-placed offers box empty.

1.0.6

  • “Only N available” beside the price replaces the generic In-stock line.

1.0.5

  • Quantity and Add to basket sit on one line.

1.0.4

  • The condition block renders beside the buy button on the deal page –
    decision information next to the decision.

1.0.3

  • Single-condition deals auto-select their condition and hide the
    chooser – the buy box loads ready.

1.0.2

  • Settings moved to WooCommerce -> RepairStep Open Box.

1.0.1

  • A placed [repairstep_open_box] shortcode now always wins over the
    automatic position.

1.0.0

  • First release: offers box (auto + shortcode) and the deal page template.
